name: Indiana
summary: A gold torch on a blue field surrounded by nineteen gold stars, with the word 'INDIANA' above. Designed by Paul Hadley for the state centennial in 1916.
origin: The Daughters of the American Revolution held a contest for the 1916 centennial. Paul Hadley's design was adopted by the General Assembly in 1917; the name was added above the torch in 1955.

symbols.name: Torch
symbols.meaning: Liberty and enlightenment; the rays show its far-reaching influence.

symbols.name: Nineteen stars
symbols.description: An outer circle of 13, an inner arc of five, and one large star above the torch.
symbols.meaning: The thirteen original states, the next five, and Indiana as the 19th state.

facts: The large star above the torch represents Indiana.
Paul Hadley was paid $100 for his design.
It is regularly ranked in the top half of state flag designs.
clues: A gold torch on blue surrounded by nineteen gold stars.
Its largest star marks the 19th state.
Designed for a state centennial in 1916.
